2609.24985.title: Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use
2609.24985.paper_summary: Multi-turn tool-use failures can hinge on a single model call, yet reward variation alone does not reveal which call would benefit from training. When rewards depend on later interactions, their variation can reflect downstream randomness rather than differences between the current actions. We introduce Critical-State RL to identify trainable states in multi-turn interactions. Given task-defined candidate calls and local rewards, the method assesses whether each reward captures the action's effect on task success and whether improvement over a reference policy is possible. It then uses nested sampling to separate action-dependent reward variation from continuation noise and optimizes the policy at the selected states using contextual-bandit training. Experiments on the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) v4 compare training at diagnostic-selected states with training at alternative states. For missing-function tasks, the diagnostic selects the response after the tool becomes available; for missing-argument tasks, it selects the response before the missing argument is supplied. Training the selected responses improves performance, including about 14 percentage points on the missing-function task, while training the alternatives leaves performance flat or worse. We further apply the recipe across models and tasks, including logged repeat-call avoidance and memory management.
2609.24985.paper_summary_zh: 多輪工具使用失敗可能取決於單一模型調用，但僅僅依賴獎勵變化並不能揭示哪一個調用會從訓練中受益。當獎勵依賴於後續互動時，它們的變化可能反映下游的隨機性，而不是當前行動之間的差異。我們引入了關鍵狀態強化學習（Critical-State RL）來識別多輪互動中的可訓練狀態。給定任務定義的候選調用和局部獎勵，該方法評估每個獎勵是否捕捉到行動對任務成功的影響，以及是否有可能在參考策略上有所改進。然後，它使用嵌套抽樣來將依賴行動的獎勵變化與延續噪聲分開，並在選定狀態下使用上下文強盜訓練來優化策略。在伯克利函數調用排行榜（BFCL）v4上的實驗比較了在診斷選擇的狀態下進行訓練與在其他狀態下進行訓練的效果。對於缺失功能任務，診斷在工具可用後選擇響應；對於缺失參數任務，則在缺失參數供應之前選擇響應。訓練選定的響應提高了性能，包括在缺失功能任務上約提高14個百分點，而訓練替代方案則使性能保持平穩或更差。我們進一步將這一方法應用於不同模型和任務，包括登錄的重複調用避免和記憶管理。
